parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime is defined by a hostile national framework: universal-exposure measures (passport/visa sex-at-birth rules, secondary screening of documents casting 'reasonable doubt' on sex, fraud-based lifetime ineligibility threats), facility restrictions across many state/provinces including criminal exposure, documented custody abuse (forced labour, sexual abuse in immigration custody, conversion-style prison policies), and state threat-framing ('radically pro-transgender' counterterrorism prioritisation). Foreign governments have issued travel advisories after detentions of their citizens. The visited state/province adds a minors' care ban, school facility ban, and no gender-identity hate-crime coverage, with only patchwork municipal protection. No execution pathway is documented, but severity (detention, stranding, abuse in custody) plus universal reach places this near the 0.25 band, slightly above it only because many exposures end in exclusion rather than imprisonment and litigation is contested.

entry_documents.exposure: Universal: visa cable directs officers to refuse on document/sex discrepancies and consider lifetime fraud findings; passports confiscated or blocked, travellers stranded abroad; case-note tag applied to refused trans applicants.
entry_documents.protection: Civil-liberties suit pending; some orders enjoined; legal-aid FAQ exists; fraud finding requires all four elements and is never automatic.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can escalate into fraud adjudication and permanent ineligibility; multiple foreign governments advise trans citizens entering.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Detentions of foreign citizens over visa issues reported; immigration custody shows forced labour, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse of trans men; national prison policy mandates conversion-style treatment, hormone removal.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Visa scrutiny or fraud suspicion routes visitors into custody with documented abusive conditions.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars trans use of government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity; 4 state/provinces criminalise certain facility use (one arrest documented, 24h men's-ward holding); visited state bans school facilities per identity.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 state/provinces plus capital district have no mapped ban; adult use not restricted state-wide in visited state; criminal trigger requires willful entry plus refusal to depart.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facility rules apply nationwide regardless of local tolerance; state rules vary by location.

care_services.exposure: Minors' care banned in 27 state/provinces including visited state (no phase-out); proposed national rules bar public insurance for under-18 care; hospitals subpoenaed for minors' records; specialised youth services shut down.
care_services.protection: Adult care access not documented as restricted for visitors.
care_services.interaction: Travelling with a trans minor exposes the family: care unavailable, records investigated, teachers criminally prosecutable for facilitating transition.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'neutralization' of 'radically pro-transgender' groups; justice department uses 'radical gender ideology' framing; cash-reward system targeting listed organisations; 190+ anti-trans bills in 2023.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Documents state counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; several orders enjoined in court.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State-level threat framing amplifies all downstream exposures: policing, prosecution, social hostility.

minors_guardians.exposure: Visiting trans minor cannot continue blockers/hormones in visited state; criminal prosecution threat against teachers facilitating social transition; school sport and facilities closed to trans girls; records subpoenaed nationally.
minors_guardians.protection: Conversion therapy banned state-wide (Sept 2024); some orders blocked in court.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardians face care denial and investigation exposure that does not apply to adults alone.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Not documented at trans-specific elevated rate for visitors; bias statistics cover sexual orientation, not gender identity; visited state hate-crime law excludes gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; some municipal ordinances and arrests/prosecutions occurred (2011 case).
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse for anti-trans violence is thin in the visited state; national coverage is theoretical for visitors.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Employment and accommodations recourse patchwork; religious-freedom statute enables refusals; appellate status of care ban unresolved; passport policy contested but allowed to take effect.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Working courts have enjoined several orders; appeals succeeded historically; employment protection via national appellate ruling and 19 municipal ordinances.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unresolved litigation means operative rules can change between booking and travel; remedies exist mainly on paper.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A's exposure is exclusion and humiliation via a conduct register with no effective remedy. This dossier's exposure is that plus criminal facility exposure, fraud-based lifetime visa bans, and documented abusive custody — materially worse, though the shared feature is universal document-based exposure without reliable remedy.

0.55-B involves discretionary secondary screening ending in refusal and return transport — administrative humiliation. Here, screening can escalate to lifetime fraud findings and detention, custody conditions include documented sexual abuse and forced labour, and state threat-framing adds a hostile layer absent at 0.55-B. Rates well below.

0.75-C shows brief detention ending with release, counsel access, and compensation remedies. This regime's custody record shows impunity for abuse, conversion-style prison policy, and remedies that are contested litigation rather than functioning recourse. The gap between 0.75-C and this rating reflects the tier-1 universal exposures and tier-2 state involvement.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is a hostile parent framework that reaches every trans visitor at entry (sex-at-birth document rules, discrepancy-refusal instructions, fraud findings) and follows them into facilities, healthcare and custody, compounded by a visited state whose own record adds a minors' care ban, school facility ban, and exclusion of gender identity from hate-crime law. State involvement is documented at tiers 1–2 of the precedence ladder: universal document exposure, criminal facility triggers with a real arrest, custodial abuse with impunity, and counterterrorism framing of pro-trans ideology. Protections — pending litigation, enjoinment of some orders, municipal ordinances — are patchwork and largely untested for visitors. Visiting with a trans minor adds care denial and investigative exposure. The result sits in the High Risk band: severe, universal, state-enforced exposure without credible street-level execution risk, but with documented detention and abuse pathways after discovery.
